reflection.text:
The call was correct because the quantitative signature was extreme and reproduced: tub_mean, tub_std and tub_glcm_contrast z +17 to +40 with nuc_solidity z -18 to -28 and nuc_dna_integrated z +19.8, plus dose-dependent tub_mean increase (rho=+1.00) and a replicate at 0.03 uM that re-voted Eg5. Protocol NSC was unanimous 4/4 with similarities 0.809-0.873, which outweighed the runner-up destabilizer similarity, consistent with Eg5 inhibition causing mitotic arrest and cell death (PMID 19351824) mediated by KIF11/Eg5 (PMID 28392145).

What was ambiguous was real: k-neighbours split 5/10 Eg5 inhibitors vs 5/10 microtubule destabilizers in e4/e8/e11, and describe_phenotype listed microtubule stabilizers alongside Eg5 inhibitors. That reflects biology and optics, not error: increased tubulin intensity/texture plus low solidity and condensed DNA is shared mitotic-arrest morphology, and low-magnification fields cannot resolve monopolar versus bipolar spindles.

Acquisition helped rather than misled: sampling mid-high (0.1 uM), high (1 uM), onset (0.03 uM) and a replicate confirmed onset and reproducibility instead of chasing one saturated well. The remaining uncertainty was appropriately kept on microtubule classes (0.12 + 0.05) and the definitive test would be spindle polarity scoring (PMID 31679979).

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

**Approve — Eg5 inhibitors, p=0.82.**

- **Top vs runner-up:** Protocol NSC is unanimous 4/4 for Eg5 inhibitors (per-well similarities 0.809–0.873), vs Microtubule destabilizers as nearest alternative class with lower mean similarity (0.747 vs 0.857 in e11). The mitotic-arrest morphology (rounded bright cells, condensed DNA, tub_mean/tub_std/tub_contrast strongly up, nuc_solidity strongly down) is shared across mitotic classes, which the phenotype report (e5) correctly flags as not resolving monopolar vs bipolar spindles — but the atlas discrimination is consistent at every well, so the runner-up does not explain the vote equally well.
- **Acquisition design:** Discriminative and replicated: mid-high (dose 5, rep 1), high (dose 7, rep 1), intermediate onset (dose 4, rep 1), plus a replicate of the active dose (dose 4, rep 2) that reproduced the profile direction (e.g. nuc_solidity z≈−18, tub increases) and again voted Eg5 despite quantitative variation in tub_mean. Effects are large (|z| up to ~40), not single-well or marginal.
- **Calibration:** 0.82 is well calibrated — decisive unanimous NSC with a clear similarity gap, tempered by the acknowledged low-magnification ambiguity among mitotic-arrest classes (0.12 + 0.05 left for the two microtubule classes). Budget is exhausted (0/4 left) and no free analysis would overturn a 4/4 vote with this margin.

## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ-C** (no PubChem record shown)

Identity check: BBBC021 gives no structure for this compound (an internal code); name matches in PubChem would be unrelated compounds, so none is shown

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Eg5 inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Eg5 inhibitors**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (4/4). The Scientist's own call was **Eg5 inhibitors** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The call was correct because the quantitative signature was extreme and reproduced: tub_mean, tub_std and tub_glcm_contrast z +17 to +40 with nuc_solidity z -18 to -28 and nuc_dna_integrated z +19.8, plus dose-dependent tub_mean increase (rho=+1.00) and a replicate at 0.03 uM that re-voted Eg5. Protocol NSC was unanimous 4/4 with similarities 0.809-0.873, which outweighed the runner-up destabilizer similarity, consistent with Eg5 inhibition causing mitotic arrest and cell death (PMID 19351824) mediated by KIF11/Eg5 (PMID 28392145).

What was ambiguous was real: k-neighbours split 5/10 Eg5 inhibitors vs 5/10 microtubule destabilizers in e4/e8/e11, and describe_phenotype listed microtubule stabilizers alongside Eg5 inhibitors. That reflects biology and optics, not error: increased tubulin intensity/texture plus low solidity and condensed DNA is shared mitotic-arrest morphology, and low-magnification fields cannot resolve monopolar versus bipolar spindles.

Acquisition helped rather than misled: sampling mid-high (0.1 uM), high (1 uM), onset (0.03 uM) and a replicate confirmed onset and reproducibility instead of chasing one saturated well. The remaining uncertainty was appropriately kept on microtubule classes (0.12 + 0.05) and the definitive test would be spindle polarity scoring (PMID 31679979).

What was right:
- Trusted unanimous NSC 4/4 for Eg5 inhibitors (0.809-0.873) over k-NN 5/5 split because per-well similarity gap favored Eg5.
- Read very large tub_mean/tub_std/tub_contrast increases with nuc_solidity decrease and nuc_dna_integrated increase as mitotic arrest, not DNA replication.
- Used intermediate dose 0.03 uM onset plus replicate and dose_response rho=+1.00 to confirm dose-dependence and reproducibility.

What was wrong or missed:
- Low-magnification describe_phenotype could not distinguish monopolar (Eg5) from bipolar (stabilizer/destabilizer) arrest, leaving stabilizers in the candidate list.
- Tubulin intensity increase alone was ambiguous and k-neighbour comparison tied Eg5 with microtubule destabilizers, so similarity margin was the only discriminator.
- Missed direct spindle-polarity evidence because no high-resolution tubulin/DNA spindle assay was acquired in the blinded run.

Proposed next experiment: High-resolution tubulin plus DNA imaging at 0.03-0.1 uM to score monopolar versus bipolar spindles, paired with an in vitro Eg5 ATPase assay versus a reference Eg5 inhibitor.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [19351824](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19351824/): K858, a novel inhibitor of mitotic kinesin Eg5 and antitumor agent, induces cell death in cancer cells. *Cancer Res* (2009) — Eg5 inhibition induces mitotic arrest and cell death, consistent with the low density and mitotic enrichment seen here (PMID 19351824).
- PMID [28392145](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28392145/): HDAC Inhibitor-Induced Mitotic Arrest Is Mediated by Eg5/KIF11 Acetylation. *Cell Chem Biol* (2017) — Eg5 dysfunction is mechanistically linked to mitotic arrest via KIF11/Eg5, supporting the arrest signature as on-target (PMID 28392145).
- PMID [31679979](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31679979/): Pyrenocine A induces monopolar spindle formation and suppresses proliferation of cancer cells. *Bioorg Med Chem* (2019) — Monopolar spindle formation is the discriminative Eg5-inhibitor phenotype that low-magnification texture cannot resolve (PMID 31679979).
